Refs #6670 · `workspace#089-profile-other-resources`

## What

Before this change, the **Other Resources** tab on a user or organisation profile only appeared for its owner. The client found the resources through `User.account` / `Organization.account`, and that field resolves to `null` for everyone else, so the client hid the tab.

This PR adds a separate, viewer-scoped field instead of opening up `account`:

```graphql
type User         { hostedResources: AccountHostedResources }   # null for anonymous
type Organization { hostedResources: AccountHostedResources }

type AccountHostedResources {
  virtualContributors: [AccountHostedVirtualContributor!]!
  innovationPacks:     [InnovationPack!]!
  innovationHubs:      [AccountHostedInnovationHub!]!
}
type AccountHostedVirtualContributor { id: UUID!  profile: Profile! }
type AccountHostedInnovationHub      { id: UUID!  nameID: NameID!  profile: Profile! }
```

Filtering happens in one place, `AccountLookupService.getHostedResourcesForViewer`. It filters on `searchVisibility` only; `listedInStore` (the "Visible in Alkemio Library" setting) is ignored on purpose:

| Viewer | VCs & Template Packs | Custom Homepages |
|---|---|---|
| Today's full-account viewers: self, `READ_USER_PII`, org `UPDATE`, `ACCOUNT_LICENSE_MANAGE` / `TRANSFER_RESOURCE_ACCEPT` on the account | everything (no regression) | all |
| Org associate / admin / owner (credential on the org) | PUBLIC + ACCOUNT | all |
| Any other registered user | PUBLIC | all |
| Anonymous | `hostedResources: null` | — |

HIDDEN items stay on the owner side only. For a user account that means the user. For an organisation it means admins and owners, who already get the full view through org `UPDATE`.

## Why the two card types are closed

- **VC card.** An org associate who is in none of the org's Spaces has no READ on an ACCOUNT VC. Returning the full `VirtualContributor` would make its non-null `profile` throw, and the null would wipe out the whole tab. The card exposes only `id` and the VC profile, which is already world-readable. Its profile is loaded through a dedicated `HostedVirtualContributorProfileLoaderCreator`, because `DataLoaderInterceptor` keys per-request loaders on `creator:parentClass` only. Reusing `ProfileLoaderCreator` would share one loader instance with `VirtualContributor.profile`, so whichever field resolved first would set the privilege check for both.
- **Hub card** (security review finding, medium, fixed in this PR). The full `InnovationHub.account` field needs only hub READ, which any viewer has. Through it, `hostedResources.innovationHubs.account.innovationPacks` returned the account's unfiltered packs and VCs, undoing the filter in the same response. Selecting `account` on the card is now a validation error, and test-suites has a regression row for it.

## What does not change

- `User.account` and `Organization.account` behave exactly as before. The gate was moved into a shared private helper, and the existing specs pass with no lines removed.
- No DDL, no migration, no authorization reset, and no change to VC, pack, hub or account authorization services.
- The schema change is additive only (0 BREAKING).

## Evidence (forge run, `specs/089-profile-other-resources`)

- **Gates:** lint, `test:ci:no:coverage` (892 files), build and schema print/sort/validate are all green.
- **Contracts:** `graphql-schema`, `hosted-resources-visibility`, `vc-card-projection-closed` and `account-gate-unchanged` all pass.
- **Live (isolated stack):**
  - full verification: 21/21 acceptance scenarios, test-suites 35/35 and gql-live 10/10;
  - regression after review fixes: it-spec 15/15, including the closed-card introspection, the hub → account validation error, and one operation that composes `VirtualContributor.profile` with the hosted cards in both field orders.
- **Review:** correctness, spec-compliance, quality and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security, plus three scoped drift re-reviews. Security verdict **pass**; the one confirmed finding (hub → account) is fixed above.
- All commits are signed.

## Tracked residuals / follow-ups

- **Hosted Spaces (#6695) are out of scope.** Org admins seeing the Spaces their org hosts needs its own decision.
- **The account id is still reachable** without the profile gate (`Space.account`, `VirtualContributor.account`, `InnovationHub.account`, and `lookup.account` returning unfiltered lists). This is pre-existing, outside this diff, and tracked with #6129.
- **An associate can see an ACCOUNT VC's card but may still be refused on the VC page**, because VC READ is unchanged. Widening VC read to associates would be a separate story.
- **`hostedResources` has no dataloader.** It is documented as single-profile use, so selecting it on a list query would cost about two lookups per row (low).
- **Full view still keys on `READ_USER_PII`**, so a space admin of a member also sees that member's HIDDEN items. This is kept for no-regression (operator ruling) and should be revisited together with #6695.
- **Schema descriptions are short** (≤ 70 chars) so the additive-only schema contract check stays mechanical. The full tier rule is in the code comments.
- **Release note:** packs and VCs default to ACCOUNT visibility, so visitors will see few resources until owners switch items to Public.

**Rollout:** merge and deploy this server PR before client-web. The new client query fails validation against an older server; in that case only the tab is hidden.

**Source:** free-text bug, no board story (reproduced locally). Follows #6699 (merged).

## Bug
A non-admin user who owns an organization can't see a private subspace that the organization has been invited to. That covers the invitation notification and anything else that reads the Space's About. Before #6699, the user's whole notifications list failed on every load because of it.

## Root cause
The `space-invitee` credential, which lets an invitee see a private Space, is issued to the **invited actor**. For an organization or a virtual contributor, that actor isn't a principal anyone signs in as. The invitation is accepted by the invitee's **account admins** (`InvitationAuthorizationService` grants them `ROLESET_ENTRY_ROLE_INVITE_ACCEPT`), and the invitation notification goes to them too. So the people asked to decide about the Space couldn't read it.

Local DB: the org held `space-invitee` on the subspace. Its owner/admin held only `organization-*` plus `account-admin` on the org's account, which matched nothing on the subspace.

## Fix
New rule: **whoever can accept the invitation can see the Space, for as long as the invitation is open.**

- `getCredentialsWithVisibilityOfSpace` adds the `ACCOUNT_ADMIN` credential of every organization and VC holding an **open** invitation (`invited` or `accepting`) on the Space's RoleSet (`RoleSetService.getAccountAdminCredentialsForOpenInvitations`). These are exactly the credentials that already hold the accept privilege, so the rule follows admin changes and needs no per-admin credential fan-out.
- The rule lives on the Space's authorization policy. So `inviteForEntryRoleOnRoleSet` (before the notifications go out), `eventOnInvitation` and `deleteInvitation` emit `SPACE_INVITATION_ACCEPTORS_CHANGED` for organization and VC invitations on a Space. A `SpaceModule` handler then resets that Space. `emitAsync` is used, so the reset has completed when the mutation returns. An event is used rather than an injection because `SpaceModule` already depends on `RoleSetModule`.
- **Deleting the invitee also resets those Spaces:** a VC (after its deletion transaction commits) or an organization (`deleteOrganizationWithPendingMemberships`). Their account admins' `account-admin` credential outlives the invitee, so without this the grant would remain.
- **Failures are surfaced:** the listener uses `suppressErrors: false`, which the library otherwise defaults to `true`. A failed reset fails the mutation rather than being logged and swallowed. The rule is derived from the persisted invitations on every reset, so any later reset of the Space reconciles it; there's no separate retry.
- An invite batch only resets for invitations it actually created, not for `ALREADY_INVITED` results.
- User invitations are unchanged.

Granting visibility through the visibility list gives these admins exactly what a user invitee gets through `space-invitee`. That's `READ_ABOUT` on a private Space, and cascading content `READ` on a public subspace. It's the same grant, not a wider one.

## Not in scope / open
- **After the organization accepts**, its admins lose visibility again, because the rule only covers open invitations and org membership grants its users nothing. The `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_SPACE_COMMUNITY_JOINED` notification to the other org admins therefore still points at a Space they can't read. #6699 now hides it rather than breaking the list. Whether a member org's admins should see the Space is a product decision.
- Same for VCs once accepted.
- Already true today: a user who **declines** keeps `space-invitee` (it's only revoked on accept). Untouched here.
- Existing open org/VC invitations get the new visibility on the next reset of their Space. Re-inviting, or an auth reset, applies it.

## Tests
- `invitation.service.spec.ts`: open-invitation query against the real xstate snapshots (invited/accepting kept, accepted/rejected excluded). Verified RED with the state filter removed.
- `role.set.service.spec.ts`: organization and VC invitees map to their accounts' `ACCOUNT_ADMIN` credentials.
- `invitation.resolver.mutations.spec.ts`: deleting an organization invitation resets the Space; deleting a user invitation doesn't.
- `space.invitation.acceptors.event.handler.spec.ts`: real `EventEmitterModule`; a failed reset rejects `emitAsync`. RED without `suppressErrors: false`.
- `role.set.resolver.mutations.membership.spec.ts`: a new org invitation resets the Space; an already-invited org doesn't. RED without the type filter.
- `virtual.contributor.service.spec.ts` / `registration.service.spec.ts`: VC and org deletion reset the Spaces they were invited to (VC after commit).

## Gates
`pnpm lint` (tsc + biome) ✅ · full vitest suite ✅ (pre-commit) · live check on the local repro: see the comments below.

Refs #6614. Split out of #6637, which keeps the delete-path fixes. This PR is only the one-off cleanup of the orphans those leaks left behind.

## Migration — `1790800000000-CleanUpOrphanedRecordsAndPolicies`

One-off and **reversible**. It deletes, in this order:
1. classifications, licenses and profiles that nothing names; their cascading children go with them;
2. the locations and storage buckets owned by the profiles deleted in step 1;
3. every authorization policy that nothing names, including the ones freed by steps 1–2.

Policies go last on purpose. The issue allows any order, and going last also catches the policies that steps 1–2 free.

### Backups and `down()`

Every deleted row is copied whole into `_orphan_cleanup_backup_<table>`. The copy happens in the same SQL statement as the delete, and every part of that statement reads the database as it was before any row is deleted. Three things are copied:
- the row itself;
- the children Postgres deletes with it (tagset, reference, visual, license_entitlement);
- every reference to it that Postgres sets to NULL, kept in `_orphan_cleanup_backup_nulled_references`. Today the only such reference is `file.tagsetId`.

The backups stay in place until the fix is confirmed. `down()` then inserts the rows back parents first, restores each nulled reference that is **still NULL** (one that was set since is left alone), and drops the backup tables.

The backup tables are not counted as names, otherwise the copies would keep the rows they copy. If a table is backed up but missing from `RESTORE_ORDER`, `up()` throws, so `down()` can never silently skip a backup.

**Follow-up:** once the fix is confirmed, a later migration drops the `_orphan_cleanup_backup_*` tables. Only `down()` drops them today.

### Safeguards
- **A row is kept while anything names it:** any foreign key, or any column carrying its id under the conventional name. The migration backup tables, e.g. `_auth_profile_backup_*.profileId`, hold such columns without an FK. Only an explicit list of each table's own cascading children is ignored, so an unknown reference keeps the row, including an owner whose key cascades. If nothing names a table at all, the migration throws instead of deleting every row.
- **There is no generic bucket or location sweep.** The Matrix media staging bucket is named only from configuration (`storage.file_service.matrix_media_bucket_id`). Only buckets and locations whose profile this migration deleted are removed.
- **Files are never deleted.** Their content lives in file-service storage, which only file-service may release. An unowned profile whose bucket holds files is left whole and counted in the log.
- **Rows created in the last day are skipped,** so an in-flight create, which saves children before their parent, cannot lose a child.
- **Only deleted ids come back to Node** (plus a deleted profile's location and bucket ids). Whole rows go from the delete straight into the backup inside Postgres, so ~15k policies' rule JSON is never held in Node memory.

## Dry run on a full dev copy of acceptance data (`up()` → `down()`, rolled back)

| | deleted | after `down()` |
|---|---|---|
| classifications | 2,997 | byte-identical |
| licenses / entitlements | 12 / 106 | byte-identical |
| profiles / locations / storage buckets | 44 / 44 / 44 | byte-identical |
| tagsets / references / visuals | 2,918 / 25 / 13 | byte-identical |
| authorization policies | 15,396 | byte-identical |
| files | 0 | byte-identical |

`up()` took ~14 s. A second run deletes nothing. 12 unowned profile trees whose buckets hold files are left for a file-service cleanup.

Of the deleted classifications, 729 are the live leak since April; the rest are 2025 rows whose policy was never computed, with no owner.

## Tests
- `clean-up-orphaned-records-and-policies.postgres.spec.ts` (10 cases) runs in the CI PostgreSQL job via `pnpm run test:migration:orphan-cleanup:postgres`, which fails rather than skips when `MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. One case runs `up()` then `down()` and expects every table to come back byte-identical, including a nulled `file.tagsetId`. Removing any one safeguard turns a specific case red; so do dropping the nulled-reference capture and dropping the backup-table exclusion.

## Deploy notes
- Rollback: `migration:revert` restores the deleted rows from the backup tables. The deploy pipeline's gated pre-migration backup remains the last resort.
- Independent of #6637 in either order. Until #6637 ships, the delete paths keep leaking, so some orphans will reappear after this runs.

## Not in this PR
- The policy leaks of the group-A delete paths and failed creates.
- File-bearing orphan trees, historical empty orphan buckets (the 813 in the issue), and orphaned aggregators/documents: these need a file-service path.
- Dropping the backup tables (follow-up, above).

## What

Tapping a native push notification now opens **the thing the notification is about**, instead of the app's start route.

`workspace#088-app-push-tap-routing` · closes alkem-io/alkemio#2193 · epic #1737 · follows `086-app-push-mvp`

`client-web` only. **No server change** — the payload has shipped the target at `notification.data.url` on both platforms since 086. **No `client-appstore` change, no new native build, no app-store round trip**: the shell is a remote-origin webview and the push plugin is already compiled into both native projects, so this rides an ordinary client-web release.

## How

Two pieces:

**`normalizePushTargetUrl(raw, origin)`** — a pure reducer from the payload's `url` to a router-usable path. It has to exist because the field is **not one shape**: `urlGeneratorService` emits an absolute `hosting.endpoint_cluster`-rooted URL for a deep link and the bare string `/` for home-link events, and the transport passes both through verbatim (086 FR-007). Anything else — a different origin, a protocol-relative authority, a non-http(s) scheme, an unparseable URL, a non-string, an empty string — returns `undefined`, which is documented as *stay on the start route*.

**`useNativePushTapRouting`** — registers `pushNotificationActionPerformed`, normalises, and navigates. Mounted from a tiny always-rendered component in `root.tsx`, inside `<BrowserRouter>` and **outside** the auth gate.

### Two structural facts that changed the shape of this change

Issue #2193 described this as a two-file edit adding a listener beside the existing two in `useNativePushRegistration`. Triage refuted that, and both corrections are load-bearing:

1. **`useNativePushRegistration` only exists while signed in.** `PushNotificationProvider` short-circuits when `!isAuthenticated`, so the inner provider never mounts — and that hook's own docblock says "mounting IS the sign-in transition". A tap listener there could never catch a **cold-start** tap, which is the main case. Hence the separate always-mounted consumer above the auth gate.

2. **`plugin.removeAllListeners()` is plugin-global.** It ran in the registration hook's cleanup on every sign-out, so it would have silently eaten the tap listener. **Ruling: narrowed the cleanup (option b).** The call is deleted, *and* `removeAllListeners` is removed from the hand-written `NativePushPlugin` type — so reintroducing it is now a **compile error**, not merely a failing test. Rejected the alternative (have the tap consumer re-register on removal) because it keeps a global instrument whose only effect is to break other consumers.

## Rulings recorded here

- **Signed-out tap → navigate immediately.** No stash, no persistence. Stashing was rejected because it would introduce the only new persisted shape in an otherwise data-free change, and the app's existing auth flow already handles an unauthenticated deep link.
- **Wrong-user tap → no client-side identity check.** Route-level authorization is the gate. A client-side entitlement decision would put a forgeable signal next to an authorization path, which `isAppMode.ts` calls a hard stop.
- **`isAppMode` third consumer, ruled in.** That file states its two legitimate consumers and that a third needs a ruling. The tap handler is the third; the docblock now records it and restates that it is not on an authorization path.

## Evidence

|---|---|
| Route | `direct` (triage; no spec — operator asked to skip it and triage independently agreed) |
| Simplification | 20 lines removed, gates green before and after |
| Typecheck | `tsc --noEmit` clean |
| Tests | **full suite 5145 passed / 2 skipped**; feature scope 33 passed across 5 files |
| Lint | the 7 new/changed files: **zero** biome findings, zero eslint findings |
| Review | 8 raw → 3 in-diff → 2 confirmed; 5 baseline (never blocking); 0 regressions in the confirm pass |
| Security verdict | `conditional` · `hold: false` |

**The simplifier earned its place.** It removed a `navigateRef` the implementer had justified, disproving the justification against the installed router: `resolveTo` keeps a leading-`/` path verbatim without consulting the captured `locationPathname`, so the stale-`navigate` guard protected an unreachable difference. **SEC-088-01 (high) — fixed in `03d472f26`.** An open redirect *in the function written to prevent open redirects*. `new URL('<origin>//evil.example/x', origin)` is **same-origin** (`origin` matches) but its pathname is `//evil.example/x`. react-router keeps that verbatim, `pushState` throws `SecurityError` for a cross-origin resolved URL, and react-router's catch **falls through to `window.location.assign()`** — it fails *open*. The original tests covered the bare `//evil.example` form but not the origin-prefixed one, so every gate was green with the hole open.

Fixed with one guard (`pathname.startsWith('//')`), a test case pinning it, and no new machinery. The adjudicator proposed downgrading this to medium and **the downgrade was refused** — a security grade cannot be lowered without the evidence a refutation requires.

**SEC-088-02 (medium) — accepted, attested, tracked as alkem-io/alkemio#2195.** Android's `MainActivity` is `exported="true"` with an `ACTION_MAIN`/`LAUNCHER` filter and Capacitor fans every launching intent to all plugins, so a notification-tap event's provenance is not verifiable from the web layer: a locally installed app can cause the signed-in webview to navigate to a route without interaction. **Confined to same-origin routes by the SEC-088-01 fix** — it was unbounded off-origin before that. **Device verification of the tap on both platforms** (the 086 HG-2 devices) is **not** reproducible in this workspace — client-web vendors no native plugin and no device is assumed — so it is surfaced, never auto-ticked. Everything above is static and unit-level.

Reported, never blocking. Notably `pnpm lint` already fails on `develop` with the same 3 warnings, in files this change touches 0 lines of. The most useful one: `PushNotificationProvider.tsx:96-98` hands the service worker's **raw, unnormalised** URL straight to `navigate()`, so the **web** push leg has the same class of defect this change fixes for native. - Desired state metalayer ([#​8432](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8432), [#​8437](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8437), [#​8439](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8439), [#​8443](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8443), [#​8452](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8452), [#​8460](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8460), [#​8476](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8476), [#​8576](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8576), [#​8598](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8598), [#​8602](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8602), [#​8603](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8603))
  - A new desired state reconciliation engine for streams and consumers considerably improves the safety and reliability of asset moves and scales
  - Updating the placement or replication factor midway through an existing scale/move operation, cancelling an in-flight scale/move, or peer-removing is now much safer
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Cancel stream move endpoint ([#​8476](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8476))
  - An in-flight scale/move operation on a stream can be cancelled and the asset returned to its original placement using the new `$JS.API.STREAM.CANCEL_MOVE` endpoint
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Evacuate endpoints ([#​8443](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8443))
  - The new `$JS.API.SERVER.EVACUATE` endpoint can safely evacuate streams, and any consumers on those streams, from a node
  - The new `$JS.API.STREAM.PEER.EVACUATE.*` endpoint can safely evacuate a peer, and any consumers on that peer, from a stream
  - These operations combined allow for maintenance operations with full transfer of data and state without having to peer-remove first
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Metalayer rescue for disaster recovery ([#​8408](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8408))
  - The new `$JS.API.META.RESCUE` endpoint can temporarily lower the quorum-needed for the metalayer, in order to facilitate the recovery of a system where nodes have been permanently lost and the metalayer cannot reach quorum
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-61.md>
- Stream backup and restore v2 ([#​7882](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/7882), [#​8584](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8584), [#​8591](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8591), [#​8604](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8604))
  - A new backup format for stream snapshots which reads out per-message rather than per-block
  - The new backup format also now correctly includes non-replicated consumers on follower nodes
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-63.md>
- Detect source stream recreation ([#​8384](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8384))
  - The server now detects a source stream being recreated, restarting the sourcing back from the beginning, ensuring new messages are sourced
- Stream source indexing ([#​8282](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8282), [#​8516](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8516), [#​8283](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8283))
  - Restarts and leader changes previously required expensive backward scans through the stream to find the last sourced indices. These are now persisted in an index for instant lookup.
- Domain-prefixed JS API in system account ([#​8429](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8429))
  - When a system account is bridged between the hub and a leaf node, the domain-prefixed JS API can now be used to operate on the leaf node while directly connected to the hub

##### Changed

JetStream

- Streams now have a default limit of 1000 consumers, unless `max_consumers` is specified in the stream config or account limits ([#​8337](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8337), [#​8566](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8566))
  - Applications planning to use a large number of consumers on a stream should configure `max_consumers` in the stream config or account limits to an appropriately high number
  - The server-wide default of 1000 can be overridden by setting `default_max_consumers` in the JetStream limits, or can be disabled by setting to `-1`
  - This limit does not affect existing consumers and will not result in consumer deletions, only the creation of new consumers is prevented
- Sync changes for replicated streams ([#​8447](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8447))
  - When the `sync_interval` is set to `always`, replicated streams now sync their WAL entries but no longer sync upper stream layer writes
  - The synced log allows the stream to recover safely, but removing unnecessary syncs from the upper stream layer dramatically improves performance
  - Non-replicated R1 streams are not affected by this change and will continue to sync at the stream layer as normal
- The `js_raft_delete_range` feature is now enabled by default ([#​8520](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8520))

Leafnodes

- The `no_advertise` option no longer includes the hub's own listener address ([#​8451](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8451), contributed by [@​freakes](https://redirect.github.com/freakes))

##### Improved

JetStream

- Shorter wait for durable source/mirror consumer resets ([#​8323](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8323))
  - When using durable consumers for sourcing or mirroring, the heartbeats now short-circuit the recreation backoff
- An atomic batch for a single-replica stream run with `sync: always` now syncs messages as a group ([#​8539](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8539), contributed by [@​RainyPixel](https://redirect.github.com/RainyPixel))
- JetStream source/mirror reply subjects can now opt-in to be domain/account aware ([#​8586](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8586), contributed by [@​ayushk-1801](https://redirect.github.com/ayushk-1801))

MQTT

- QOS 1 published into JetStream are pipelined for increased throughput ([#​8415](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8415), contributed by [@​levb](https://redirect.github.com/levb))

##### Fixed

Leafnodes

- Leafnode isolation using `request_isolation`, or with hub-enforced `isolate`, now works correctly across cluster nodes ([#​8504](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8504))

## ⚠️ MERGE ORDER IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT A PREFERENCE

**Merge and deploy alkem-io/server#6667 to the shared test cluster BEFORE merging this.**

`server-api/vitest.config.ts` puts `src/functional-api/callout/**` in the **`nightly`** project, which runs against the shared cluster. From the moment this file lands on `develop`, the nightly executes it — **fixture writes included** — and reports it red until the server slice is deployed there.

The remedy is merge order, not confinement: a "assert `ALKEMIO_SERVER` is localhost" pre-flight would red the nightly *by construction*, since the nightly deliberately targets the shared cluster. This is stated in the file's own header. If the order cannot be held, the nightly is **knowingly red** for this spec — and the slice contract forbids buying the window with a `skip`.

## Why this repo is in the feature at all

Because nothing else could prove the central claim. `vitest` runs `environment: 'node'` with hand-wired repository mocks and **no Postgres**, so every server unit assertion restates its own mock. `SC-002` requires the account boundary be exercised "against a real account boundary at least once" — this suite is that once, and it is the only place the SQL join is not restated by the thing testing it.

## The six cases

1. `AC4`/`FR-003` — a foreign-account id is **rejected on create**, nothing persisted
2. `AC4`/`FR-003b` — a **newly added** foreign id is rejected on update, the stored list untouched
3. `AC7` — an id that **left the account** is dropped silently, the save succeeds
4. `AC1`/`FR-004a`/`FR-017` — a cross-L0 same-account space **and** the host's own L2 are accepted, persisted, and the collection renders whole
5. `AC2`/`FR-010` — `accountSpaces` offers every level and **never** the foreign space
6. `AC3`/`FR-009` — `accountSpaces` is refused to an actor holding `READ` but not `UPDATE`

**Case 4 is the load-bearing one.** Every L1/L2 row's own `accountId` is NULL (`account` is assigned only at `SpaceLevel.L0`; `createSubspace` propagates `levelZeroSpaceID` and never touches `account`). So a predicate spelled `space."accountId" = <host account>` returns the empty set for the sibling L1, the write guard rejects it, and case 4 goes **red**. It passed twice — so the executed SQL must resolve the account through `levelZeroSpaceID`. That is the defect this suite exists to catch, disproven by execution rather than by reading code.

Verified: **6/6 passing, twice, exit 0**, against a stack carrying the server slice.

## Evidence

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| Triage | route `spec`; **3 of the issue's own premises refuted** |
| Spec | accepted after 3 attempts (21→13 blocking); net-subtractive |
| Build | 7 chunks green, cross-repo contract passed first round, simplifier −116 lines |
| Verify | it-spec **6/6 twice** (`SC-002` satisfied against real Postgres) · walks **US1 10/10, US2 3/3** |
| Review | 2 full funnel rounds + 1 scoped: 67 raw → 31 actionable → all fixed, 0 regressions |

**Verification highlights.** `AC1` proven with a genuine negative: the picker offered the host, its L1, its L2, a sibling L0 of the account and a subspace under it, while a space on a *different* account — one the admin provably holds `READ` on — never appeared under any query, so the scoping is by **account**, not by read access. `AC8` proven in its hardest form: with `selectedIds` holding a sibling L0 and a deep L2 but `mode: AUTO`, the collection still rendered only the host's own subspace, with no notice. Both `D3` regressions hold — `CUSTOM→AUTO→CUSTOM` preserves the stored selection, and an unrelated Contributors-callout edit leaves its contributor selection intact.

## What review caught that nothing else would have

- **`SEC-084-01`** — the account-wide SPACES selection was writable by a **non-admin**. The create path gates SPACES framing behind space-admin `CREATE`; the update path's "mirror" of that guard covered `CONTRIBUTORS` only. A plain member could create a POST callout (they hold `UPDATE` on their own callout, and `allowMembersToCreateCallouts` maps `CREATE_CALLOUT`→`CONTRIBUTE`), convert it to SPACES, and publish an account-portfolio-wide collection — the capability `AC3` reserves for a host-space admin. Fixed subtractively by routing the update path through the create path's own helper.
- **`SEC-084-CW-01`** — `AC6`'s privacy design was defeated on the same page: `selectedIds` was served to every viewer, so a non-member could diff it against the rendered `framing.subspaces` and recover the exact hidden **count** and the **UUIDs** withheld from them. Fixed in two places — GraphQL, and the MCP callout resource, which was emitting the entire raw `settings` jsonb under a READ-only gate reachable with an ordinary browser cookie.
- A **permanently-red test** added beyond its brief and auto-enrolled in the shared-cluster nightly — deleted.

## Open items for a human

- **`ac4-literal-wording` (open gate).** Built as A11: a *newly added* out-of-account id is **rejected**; a *carried-over* id that has left the account is **silently dropped** and the save succeeds. This resolves a real contradiction between `AC4` ("reject any") and `AC7` ("omitted on save") in `AC7`'s favour. The strict reading of `AC4` is purely **additive** on top if you want it.
- **Two refused severity downgrades.** The adjudicator argued `SEC-084-01` down to medium (curation, not exposure — the read path still filters per viewer) and `SEC-084-TS-01` down to low (30 existing specs already flip fixtures to PUBLIC in the nightly). Both were **refused and held** at the higher grade, because lowering a security grade is risk acceptance. Yours to grade.

- **Pre-existing, filed as baseline:** `Account.spaces` is readable unfiltered by any viewer with `READ` on one space of the account; automatic mode still performs no list-level filtering and is exposed to the same whole-collection nullification. Neither is this feature's to fix — both deserve their own tickets.

### 2. Whiteboard E2E → local-first editor (close-to-save)

The whiteboard editor rework (client-web#10205/#10207/#10241 era) changed the contract: the editor dialog is named after the whiteboard (the `Drawing canvas` filter text no longer exists), the **Save button is gone** (autosave + durable close via *Close whiteboard*), *Find Template* moved to the editor header, and materializing a template's drawing renames the outer dialog Create→"Edit whiteboard template".

### 3. Callout full-workflow spec → worker- and retry-safe

`0.1callout-full-workflow.spec.ts` chained five steps across three fixture describes on module-level `Date.now()` callout names. That only holds when every describe runs in the same worker: local `fullyParallel` can split them, a retry always gets a fresh worker (fresh module eval => fresh name), and running a single step in isolation never runs the sibling that created the entity.

- The admin-created callout name is assigned in the Step 1/2 `beforeAll` (one serial worker) instead of at module level.
- The outer `beforeAll` seeds a **published** callout via `createCalloutOnCalloutsSet`; Steps 3–5 open that instead of the Step-1 UI callout, so any subset of tests works in any worker.

Durable Playwright cover for **workspace#051-cleverbase-account-linking** — the Connected Accounts section on Security settings, shipped in alkem-io/client-web#10176 (merged to `develop` 2026-08-24).

The forge run's Phase-V acceptance walks were driven ad-hoc and **persisted no specs** — its own ledger recorded *"Emitted @forge-acceptance specs: none persisted … the durable-spec follow-up can ride the test-suites flow."* This is that follow-up.

## Coverage — 13 cases, 7 files

`client-web/src/functional-e2e/connected-accounts/`

| Case | What it pins |
|---|---|
| CA-01 | three provider rows *Not connected* + Connect, read-only credential rows, no identity leakage |
| CA-02 | credential rows route via in-page anchors to the password/passkey cards, no inline mutation |
| CA-05 | a password error stays inside the password card (does not echo into the section) |
| CA-06 | owner-only: a platform admin on another user's security URL is redirected, no settings flow created |
| CA-04 | fail-closed when the settings flow is unreadable — explicit error + retry, **zero** provider rows; retry recovers in place |
| CA-03 / CA-07 | last-method lock shows a focusable `aria-disabled` Disconnect carrying its reason; curing the lock flips the same row to enabled |
| CA-30 / CA-31 | disconnect requires the confirm dialog — confirming POSTs `unlink=<provider>` with zero provider contact, Cancel fires no POST |
| CA-20 / CA-21 | Connect natively POSTs `link=<provider>` + CSRF to the flow action and writes the outcome marker; returning from an interrupted Connect announces the retry notice once |
| CA-40 / CA-42 / CA-43 / CA-43b | errored-flow resume (`4000007`) on bare `/settings`, and each outcome announcement — pending, connected, disconnected — exactly once |
| CA-41 | regression: the recovery-born settings flow still renders *Set new password* on bare `/settings` (the T027 resume seam) |

Live dev stack throughout; Kratos settings-flow **reads** are mocked only where a state cannot be provoked deterministically (locked rows, unreadable flow, completed round-trips). All URLs resolve at runtime from each persona's own profile URL — never a hardcoded `/user/<slug>`.

## Harness changes these depend on

- **`authenticated-session.fixture.ts`** — persona sessions are validated against Kratos `whoami` before reuse, and gain `maxSessionAgeSeconds`. Kratos gates privileged self-service operations behind `privileged_session_max_age` (15m); a live-but-stale cached session makes a privileged submit redirect to a re-auth screen instead of returning the expected settings-flow response. Specs doing privileged work now re-mint rather than mis-assert.
- **`config/global-setup.ts`** — provision personas through the Kratos **admin** API when `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` is reachable (deterministic; no HIBP/self-service policy; a reset Kratos store heals on the next run instead of timing out every login), falling back to self-service registration otherwise. Then warm every persona's storage state **serially, before any worker exists** — concurrent cold logins were blowing the 30s budget as `Test timeout … exceeded while setting up storageState`. Warm-up failures are deliberately non-fatal so only the affected specs go red, attributably.
- **`getRecoveryLink(recipientEmail?)`** — the MailSlurper inbox is shared. An unfiltered subject match could open **another suite's** recovery mail and complete recovery against it, silently resetting that persona's harness credential for the rest of the run. `authentication-password-recovery.spec.ts` updated to pass its own address.

## Gates

- `tsc --noEmit` clean — `client-web` and `lib`
- `eslint` clean on every new/changed file
- Commit GPG-signed

## Run results — 15 / 16 green

Run against the local dev stack (client-web on `develop` incl. the merged #10176; Traefik origin `:3000`), `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` set so `global-setup` provisions personas through the Kratos admin API.

| Run | Workers | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (3.1m) |
| 2 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (1.9m) |
| 3 | 1 | 15 passed, 1 failed (2.2m) |

The 15 are stable and fast (1.5-4.7s each) across all three runs — every case that exercises Connected Accounts itself is green.

### The one failure is NOT a test defect and NOT 051

**CA-41** times out at its first UI step, waiting for `Forgot password?`, with the login page frozen on *"Preparing secure sign-in…"*. Root cause reproduced with **zero test code involved** — a bare fresh browser context hitting `/login` directly:

```
401 /api/auth/oidc/id-token-hint | 302 /api/auth/oidc/login | 302 /oidc/login
303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE
403 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/flows?id=...
{"error":{"id":"security_csrf_violation","code":403, ...}}
```

Two defects, both on the **login/OIDC bootstrap** — a surface 051 does not touch:

1. The login flow is created **twice** in one cold sign-in; the SPA then fetches the flow id from the URL while the anti-CSRF cookie has moved on, and Kratos rejects it with `security_csrf_violation`.
2. On that 403 the SPA **hangs indefinitely** on "Preparing secure sign-in…" — no error surfaced, no retry, no recovery.

Reproduction rate on this stack was high but not total (one fresh context in an early batch of three succeeded; a later batch of four failed 4/4), which is what made CA-41 look flaky before the cause was isolated.

This is the same *class* of bug the 051 review already fixed on the settings page ("settings flow created before `profileUrl` resolved — double flow creation, lost `return_to`"); this is the login page's version of it, and it is pre-existing.

**CA-41 is a regression guard for pre-existing recovery behaviour**, so it never reaches the 051 code under test. It should not gate this PR's assessment of the feature, but it does need a decision: fix the login bootstrap, or make CA-41 tolerate a stale flow id.

### Still manual

The 8 off-site OAuth round-trips (LinkedIn/Microsoft/GitHub) from the original walk stay out of automation; the provider hop is asserted up to the redirect only.

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  ## Raised separately

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.
